claim: Three-quarters of Twitch accounts that earned any payout in 2021 (through September) made less than $120.
stance_target: Measured-telemetry estimates of creator earnings show the vast majority of monetized creators earn near-negligible amounts
scope_conditions: Twitch, January-September 2021, denominator excludes ~896,261 accounts with zero/negative revenue; based on an unverified leaked dataset of ~4.9 million accounts
quoted_support: While a small pool of streamers have taken home seven-figure shares of that pool, three-quarters of users making any money this year have made less than $120.
time_period: January-September 2021 (payout data traces back to July 2019)

claim: Half of all Twitch streamers who earn payouts made less than $28 in 2021 through September.
stance_target: Median creator earnings on major platforms are far below any living-wage threshold
scope_conditions: Twitch, January-September 2021, only accounts with nonzero payout counted; Twitch requires a $100 accrued balance before issuing any payout, which right-censors low earners in a given window
quoted_support: Half of all streamers who earn payouts have made less than $28 so far this year, a far cry from top earners' millions. However, Twitch only offers payouts once a streamer's accrued revenue balance reaches $100.

claim: Only 0.06% of the leaked Twitch accounts received payouts exceeding the U.S. median household income of $67,521.
stance_target: Direct measured-telemetry evidence that the share of creators reaching a living-wage-comparable income threshold is on the order of a few hundredths of a percent, consistent with the 0.04-1.6% telemetry-based estimates in the broader corpus
scope_conditions: Twitch, ~4.9 million leaked accounts, through 2021; benchmark is U.S. median HOUSEHOLD income, not an individual living wage, and not adjusted for the fact that payouts are gross of Twitch's revenue share and exclude non-Twitch income sources
quoted_support: Exceedingly few are getting rich from streaming: Only 0.06% received over the U.S. median household income of $67,521.
region: United States benchmark applied to a global platform population

claim: The top 1% of Twitch streamer accounts earned over half of all money paid out in 2021, and the top 1,000 accounts alone earned a quarter of all revenue ($220 million of $889 million).
stance_target: Creator earnings on major platforms follow an extreme power-law/superstar distribution
scope_conditions: Twitch payouts, January-September 2021, ~4.0 million earning accounts
quoted_support: The top 1% of Twitch streamers made over half of all money paid out in 2021, according to a Wall Street Journal analysis of data made public in a high-profile leak. ... A quarter of all revenue was earned by the top 1,000 accounts.

claim: Only 5% of Twitch users in the leaked dataset made over $1,000 in 2021.
stance_target: A very small share of monetized creators cross even a low four-figure annual earnings threshold, let alone a living wage
scope_conditions: Twitch, through September 2021, excludes zero-revenue accounts
quoted_support: Only 5% of users have made over $1,000 this year

claim: Twitch's total streamer payouts nearly tripled in under two years, reaching roughly $100 million per month by 2021, up from $517 million total over Jan-Sept 2020 to $889 million over the same window in 2021.
stance_target: Growth trajectory of platform-mediated creator payouts during the pandemic period
scope_conditions: Twitch payout data from July 2019 through September 2021
quoted_support: In just under two years, the amount paid out to streamers has almost tripled to around $100 million a month.

claim: The WSJ's percentile and dollar figures are derived from an unverified leak; the paper independently cross-referenced one streamer's pay stubs against the leaked records and found month totals matched within 25 cents, but stated it could not independently verify the leaked data as a whole.
stance_target: Reliability/provenance caveat for any downstream use of these percentile figures
scope_conditions: Single cross-reference case; leak originated from a 4chan user claiming access to internal Twitch systems; Twitch (Amazon) confirmed a server misconfiguration exposed some data but did not validate the leak's completeness or accuracy
quoted_support: The Journal cross-referenced pay stubs from one streamer against the same records in the leaked data and found most months' payout totals matched within 25 cents. The WSJ hasn't been able to independently verify the leaked data.

claim: The WSJ figures cover only Twitch-mediated payouts (subscriptions and advertising via the platform) and explicitly exclude other creator income sources such as corporate sponsorships, tipping services, and video-game publisher payments.
stance_target: Twitch payout percentiles alone represent total creator income
quoted_support: These figures don't include other possible income sources such as corporate sponsors, tipping services and videogame publishers.
